statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of four public archetypes plus a 404 recovery state. Authenticated member-only areas, payments, account cancellation execution, livestream playback and actual account creation were not covered because they require credentials, personal data or commitment.

page.framework: Mixed server-rendered pages with custom elements/client-rendered islands

paths.description: Public landing page and primary acquisition surface; inspected desktop, mobile, user preferences, load, network, security, accessibility, discoverability and memory.
Representative listing/filter template and event-discovery journey; inspected desktop, mobile and no-JavaScript rendering.
Representative content/index surface with high public-discoverability value; inspected desktop, mobile and crawler/no-JavaScript rendering.
Primary registration form; inspected field semantics, autofill, invalid submission behaviour, mobile layout and no-JavaScript rendering without creating an account.
Representative HTTP/error recovery state at an intentionally invalid URL.

findings.summary: Theme does not respond to the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Dark-emulated and default screenshots are byte-identical (402,610 bytes), while the probe reports matchMedia dark=true but no prefers-color-scheme/light-dark CSS and color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven light/dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Motion is unchanged when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Both probes report three running 200 ms animations; the reduced-motion probe finds no prefers-reduced-motion CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override that removes non-essential carousel and transition motion.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not explicitly supported.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules and the prefers-contrast screenshot is byte-identical to default.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for controls, focus indicators and muted text.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules on a site with many MPA routes and changing carousel state.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin routes and important state changes with View Transitions, retaining instant navigation as fallback.

findings.summary: The hero carousel is JS-driven without platform scroll-snap/gesture semantics.
findings.evidence: The landing screenshot shows carousel arrows and dots, while CSS inspection found no scroll-snap signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a horizontal scroll-snap carousel with native touch/keyboard scrolling and progressive arrow controls.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation does not expose scroll-aware feedback.
findings.evidence: Desktop and long mobile captures show static header chrome; CSS inspection found neither scroll-state queries nor scroll timelines.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained scroll-state feedback, such as a compact sticky header or progress cue, without obscuring content.

findings.summary: Several controls and overlay surfaces use custom elements instead of native primitives.
findings.evidence: Registration uses J-BUTTON custom elements; the landing DOM has a role=dialog surface but no dialog, popover or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native button, dialog, popover and details primitives, preserving accessible names and built-in dismissal/focus behaviour.

findings.summary: Some interactive targets are too short for reliable touch use.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe found several links only 15–16 px high, including story and business-registration links.
findings.suggestedFix: Give interactive targets a minimum 44×44 CSS pixel activation area while preserving visible keyboard focus.

findings.summary: The registration flow hides requirements from browser semantics and cannot be safely validated before navigation.
findings.evidence: All visible registration fields report required=false; the custom submit immediately navigated/closed the inspected target on an empty submission, preventing an in-place recoverable validation state.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark required fields with native required/constraints, validate after interaction, and keep the user on the form with clear recovery until inputs are valid.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.6 s, FCP 3.1 s, Speed Index 10.6 s and performance 0.65; trace LCP was 3.00 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, reduce document latency and redirects, and defer non-critical work.

findings.summary: The critical resource chain is large and render-blocking.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 210 requests and 2.95 MB transferred, including 23 stylesheets and 159 scripts; Lighthouse estimates 1.06 s render-blocking savings and 950 ms font-display savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Bundle critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, optimise font-display and preload only the actual LCP resource.

findings.summary: The landing page ships substantial unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 239 KiB unused JavaScript and 92 KiB unused CSS; one 144 KiB chunk is 95.6% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split assets, remove legacy/global bundles from the landing template and conditionally load feature code.

findings.summary: Some controls and links have incorrect or missing accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a visible “Deutsch” control named only “Sprache ändern” and a footer logo link with no discernible accessible text.
findings.suggestedFix: Make accessible names include visible labels and name image-only links with aria-label or real text.

findings.summary: The landing template lacks clear semantic page landmarks.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found only a footer landmark on the landing page, with no main, nav or header element, despite extensive navigation and content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use header/nav/main/footer landmarks and retain the existing logical heading order and visible focus styles.

findings.summary: Small targets weaken reflow and touch accessibility.
findings.evidence: At 360 px the layout reflows without overflow, but the target probe reports multiple interactive links only 15–16 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase activation areas to at least 44×44 CSS pixels and retest at 200% zoom and 320–360 px widths.

findings.summary: Multiple images omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: Image audit found five images without width/height; Lighthouse identified four visible unsized images including app-store badges and the claim image.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width and height or aspect-ratio on every content image and preserve intrinsic aspect ratios.

findings.summary: The page emits platform deprecation warnings and ships broken source-map references.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three deprecated API warnings from the challenge script and many first-party .map URLs returning 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or isolate deprecated challenge code and publish valid source maps or remove broken sourceMappingURL declarations.

findings.summary: A valuable public content surface is nearly empty without JavaScript, and robots blocks Lighthouse crawling.
findings.evidence: Sex Education has only 2% raw/rendered word coverage, no raw H1 and isJsShell=true; Lighthouse also reports robots.txt blocking its crawler.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the Sex Education heading and core cards/links, and ensure robots.txt permits intended search and AI crawlers.

findings.summary: Representative public pages lack share-preview and entity metadata.
findings.evidence: Metadata probes found no Open Graph tags on home, events, education or signup; events and education also expose no JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter cards and relevant schema.org JSON-LD for organization, event and educational content.

findings.summary: Browser policy coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers include CSP, HSTS, nosniff and frame protection, but Permissions-Policy is missing and Referrer-Policy is the permissive legacy no-referrer-when-downgrade value.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and use strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy.

findings.summary: Registration exposes password-only authentication with no passkey path.
findings.evidence: The signup probe found a password field with empty autocomplete and no passkey/WebAuthn affordance in the inspected registration surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration/authentication as the preferred path, retaining password fallback with correct autocomplete tokens.

findings.summary: Core Sex Education content is not progressively enhanced.
findings.evidence: Crawler/no-JS capture shows only navigation and a blank content area; discoverability reports 2% content coverage and no raw H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Render core educational content and links in server HTML, then hydrate filters and richer interactions as enhancements.

findings.summary: Registration does not expose native, accessible invalid-state semantics.
findings.evidence: Every visible field reports required=false and aria-invalid is absent; empty custom submission navigates rather than yielding a stable in-place validation state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native constraints plus :user-invalid, aria-describedby and an announced error summary after submit or field interaction.

findings.summary: Sign-up fields omit expected autofill tokens.
findings.evidence: Username, password and email fields have empty autocomplete values; only hidden/decoy fields carry username/new-password tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Put username, new-password, email, bday and address-level tokens on the actual user-editable controls.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and misses responsive optimisation.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 11/12 images without srcset, nine legacy-format images, two oversized images and ten below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP sources, lazy-load below-fold media and size assets to their rendered dimensions.

findings.summary: The landing page eagerly loads both desktop and mobile hero variants plus broad code bundles.
findings.evidence: HAR offenders include four desktop and four mobile hero JPEGs on one load; Lighthouse reports 239 KiB unused JS and 92 KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Use picture/media selection so only one hero variant downloads, and conditionally import route/feature code.

findings.summary: The initial media/script budget is disproportionate to the landing task.
findings.evidence: HAR records 2.95 MB across 210 requests, including 1.72 MB images, 842 KB scripts and 159 script requests before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a landing-page budget, defer non-visible media and non-essential analytics, and consolidate/cache static assets.

Optimise responsive image delivery and dimensions
Strengthen browser security policies and authentication
Add structured/share metadata to entity pages
Modernise navigation, carousel and semantic controls
